name: What is ML? Types of ML
description: Learn the definition of Machine Learning and understand Supervised, Unsupervised, and Reinforcement learning paradigms.

name: Linear Regression — Concept, Formula, Use Case
description: Understand the most fundamental regression algorithm, the line equation y = mx + c, and gradient descent optimization.

name: Logistic Regression
description: Transition from regression to classification using the Sigmoid activation function to predict probability scores.

name: Decision Trees & Random Forest
description: Learn how trees split data using Entropy and Gini impurity, and how Random Forests average multiple trees.

name: KNN — Concept and Distance Metrics
description: Master instance-based classification and distance metrics like Euclidean, Manhattan, and Minkowski distances.

name: SVM — Concept and Kernel Trick
description: Explore support vectors, hyperplanes, margins, and mapping non-linear data using kernel functions.

name: K-Means Clustering
description: Dive into unsupervised learning, cluster centroids, inertia, and the elbow method to group unstructured data.

name: Neural Networks Basics
description: Understand artificial neurons, layers, forward propagation, weights, biases, and backpropagation.

name: Overfitting vs Underfitting
description: Analyze bias-variance trade-offs and learn regularization methods (L1/L2) to improve model generalization.

name: Evaluation Metrics
description: Learn how to measure performance using Confusion Matrix, Accuracy, Precision, Recall, F1-Score, and ROC-AUC.

name: What is AI? AI vs ML vs DL
description: Distinguish between Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, and Deep Learning fields and history.

name: Search Algorithms (BFS, DFS)
description: Learn how AI agents traverse path spaces using Breadth-First and Depth-First searching techniques.

name: Heuristic Search (A* Algorithm)
description: Optimize search paths using heuristic cost functions to estimate remaining distance to target.

name: Knowledge Representation
description: Represent facts and logic patterns using Semantic Networks, Propositional Logic, and Ontologies.

name: Natural Language Processing Basics
description: Learn text tokenization, bag-of-words, TF-IDF representations, and parts-of-speech parsing.

name: Generative AI Concepts
description: Explore the revolution of GANs, VAEs, and modern Transformer-based Large Language Models.

name: Prompt Engineering Fundamentals
description: Master structured prompting techniques including Few-Shot, Chain-of-Thought, and Role Prompting.

name: RAG — Retrieval Augmented Generation
description: Connect LLMs to external vector databases to retrieve relevant context before generation.

name: AI Ethics and Bias
description: Address critical questions about model fairness, representation, training data bias, and safety.

name: Arrays and Strings
description: Master memory contiguity, indexing, two-pointer techniques, and sliding window manipulations.

name: Linked Lists
description: Implement pointers, node structures, singly/doubly linked lists, and traversal algorithms.

name: Stacks and Queues
description: Explore Last-In-First-Out (LIFO) and First-In-First-Out (FIFO) linear data structures and applications.

name: Trees and Binary Trees
description: Master binary trees, tree traversals (In-order, Pre-order, Post-order), and BST operations.

name: Graphs
description: Learn to represent connections with Adjacency Matrices and Lists, and traverse using BFS/DFS.

name: Hashing
description: Understand hash tables, key-value mappings, hash functions, and collision resolution techniques.

name: Sorting Algorithms
description: Study sorting logic: Bubble, Insertion, Selection, Merge Sort, and Quick Sort complexities.

name: Searching Algorithms
description: Compare Linear Search and Binary Search in sorted arrays, understanding the divide-and-conquer approach.

name: Dynamic Programming Basics
description: Learn to optimize recursive problems through memoization, tabulation, and identifying overlapping subproblems.

name: Time and Space Complexity
description: Use Big O notation to analyze algorithms and evaluate execution speeds and memory footprints.
